c: Get back exactly what you had, and quickly
Rebuild stronger, not identically
Start again big with a big loan to catch up on everything
Wait for a miracle without changing anything
qcm.e: If the fall came from loans, you start again without a loan. If it came from a single client, you will have several. If it came from mixing accounts, you separate the money from day one.

exercices.consigne: Four guided calculations with invented figures, then the price of your own product. Reread the lesson “Managing your business”.

champs.label: A jar of jam costs in variable costs: fruit 300 F, jar 200 F, sugar 60 F, label 40 F. It sells for 1,000 F. What is the margin per jar?
champs.explication: Variable costs: 300 + 200 + 60 + 40 = 600 F. Margin = selling price − variable costs = 1,000 − 600 = 400 F.

champs.label: Fixed costs are 45,000 F per month (including your salary). What is the break-even point?
champs.explication: 45,000 ÷ 400 = 112.5, that is about 113 jars. Below that, you lose money.

champs.label: You sell 300 jars in the month. What is the profit?
To attract clients, you lower the price from 1,000 F to 900 F (−10%). What happens to your margin per jar?
options: It falls by 25%: 300 F instead of 400 F
champs.bonne: It falls by 25%: 300 F instead of 400 F
champs.explication: A 10% reduction on the price cuts much more than 10% of the margin. Before a discount, redo the calculation. But never go below your cost price.

champs.label: The price of my product or service
champs.aide: Fill in the four lines for a product or service that you sell or want to sell. The three results are calculated automatically.

exercices.consigne: Read a cash flow table, do your invoice calculations, learn to follow up with a client methodically and prepare your invoice template. Reread the lessons “Invoicing” and “Getting paid”.

champs.label: Month 2: you have 50,000 F at the start, 200,000 F comes in and 320,000 F goes out. How much do you have at the end of the month?
champs.explication: 50,000 + 200,000 − 320,000 = − 70,000 F. Over three months the business earns money, but in month 2 some is missing.

champs.label: You see this gap in advance. What do you do?
options: Nothing: it will sort itself out in month 3
I ask for a deposit, I delay a purchase or I negotiate a delay with a supplier
I take from my personal rent money
I lend the till to the family
champs.bonne: I ask for a deposit, I delay a purchase or I negotiate a delay with a supplier
champs.explication: A three-month cash flow table is for that. Also keep a reserve of one to three months of fixed expenses.

champs.label: Invoice: 25 juices at 1,500 F and 20 jams at 1,200 F. A deposit of 15,000 F has already been received. What is the balance to pay?
Your business is subject to VAT (18%). You sell for 100,000 F excluding tax. How much does the client pay?
champs.explication: 100,000 + 18,000 = 118,000 F. The 18,000 F is passed on to the State: it is not your money.

champs.label: A friend asks you for a “favor invoice” with an inflated price, to do him a favor.
options: I accept once, to do a favor
I refuse: it is fraud, and it dishonors the name of Christ
I accept if he pays me
I accept if the amount is small
champs.bonne: I refuse: it is fraud, and it dishonors the name of Christ
champs.explication: “A false balance is an abomination to Yahweh, but accurate weights are his delight” (Prov 11:1).

champs.label: The client has not paid the day after the deadline. What do you do first?
options: I send a formal notice and go see a lawyer
I send a polite message asking him to confirm the payment date
I talk to his neighbors so that he is ashamed
I do nothing, he will pay one day
champs.bonne: I send a polite message asking him to confirm the payment date
champs.explication: A few days before: friendly reminder. The next day: polite message. One week later: call, with a precise date noted. Fifteen days: firm letter. Stay polite, firm and regular.

champs.label: One month after the due date, still nothing. What do you do?
options: I keep delivering so as not to upset him
I send a last letter (formal notice), I stop delivering and I seek advice from a lawyer or a bailiff
I threaten the client in public
champs.bonne: I send a last letter (formal notice), I stop delivering and I seek advice from a lawyer or a bailiff
champs.explication: The law provides a simple procedure to recover a clear debt: the order to pay. Keep the quote, purchase order, delivery note, invoice and messages: they are your proof.

exercices.consigne: Six offers: alert or possible serious investment after verification? Then a last question on the three buckets.

champs.label: A brother from church tells you: “Double your money in a month, it is guaranteed, God multiplies!”
options: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.bonne: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.explication: Huge and quick gain, “guaranteed”, and religious trust used as proof. Faith is shared, financial trust is verified (1 Tim 6:9).

champs.label: An SGI approved by the CREPMF gives you its written rates. You open a securities account in your name and each month you buy shares of several companies, for at least five years.
options: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.explication: Approved and verifiable intermediary, known fees, diversification, regularity, long term. Nothing is guaranteed, but the approach is sound.

champs.label: A “trading robot” website promises automatic gains, asks you to send the money to a personal Mobile Money number, and the offer ends tomorrow.
options: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.bonne: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.explication: Time pressure, money sent to a personal number, automatic gains: three signs of a scam, and the word “crypto” often hides pyramids.

champs.label: A term deposit in an approved bank, at a fixed interest known in advance, locked until the date.
options: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.explication: Very low risk. The money is locked until the date: use it for money you do not need before.

champs.label: You are offered a commission for each friend you bring into the “program”.
options: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.bonne: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.explication: If you are paid to recruit other people, it is a pyramid: the first ones are paid with the money of the next ones. See ICC Services, 2010.

champs.label: Treasury bonds bought through your bank or an SGI, after asking for the rate of the latest issue, the term and the fees.
options: Alert: I do not put in a franc
champs.explication: Generally one of the safest investments, because it is the State that repays. “Safer” does not mean “without risk”.

champs.label: You invest 40,000 F per month. What maximum sum do you put in the “bet” bucket (5% at most)?
champs.explication: 5% of 40,000 F = 2,000 F. It is a sum you accept to lose entirely. Example of a split for a cautious person: about 60% security, 35% growth, 5% bet.

champs.label: I have noted the five questions of the test and I ask them before putting in a franc: who is behind the offer and is he approved? How does it produce money? Who guarantees the capital?
